title: Mask strip control pack - grow/shrink, edge bands, alpha brushes
description:
User request 2026-07-29. One slider that dilates or erodes the current mask: drag right to grow, left to shrink. Every masking method benefits - a YOLO box is always slightly tight, a SAM edge is often a pixel proud, and the MPI-381 black-and-white view now makes both obvious. Belongs in the shared MpiMaskStrip, so it lands on every tool at once.

FEASIBILITY (checked while carding, NOT yet proven live):

LEADING CANDIDATE - client-side, real-time. Blur plus an alpha threshold IS a morphological dilate or erode: blur by r, then threshold alpha at 0.5 and the white region grows by about r; threshold above 0.5 and it shrinks. Canvas2D takes CSS filters, so the blur is one line (ctx.filter = 'blur(Npx)'). The threshold is the only interesting part: contrast() will not do it because it acts on colour, not alpha, and our mask layers are white-on-transparent. Use an inline SVG filter referenced as ctx.filter = 'url(#id)' with feComponentTransfer plus feFuncA type=discrete - Electron is Chromium, so this is available. At the MASK_MAX_EDGE working size (1536) this is a single pass and should hold a live drag.

FALLBACK if that misbehaves: per-pixel distance transform in a worker, or accept apply-on-release and reuse sharp server-side. Sharp already blurs a mask for the MPI-362 composite (services/imageComposite.js, the feather sigma), so the server path exists - but it is a round trip per drag and therefore NOT real time. Do not start there.

THE TRAP THAT WILL BITE - COMPOUNDING. The slider must always derive from a PRISTINE copy of the layer taken when the drag started, never from the last frame it produced. Feeding each frame back in means grow 3 applied three times, which eats detail exactly like the MPI-351 double-scale bug. Snapshot on pointerdown, recompute from the snapshot on every input, bake once on release.

DESIGN QUESTION to settle first: WHICH layer grows. maskCanvas is derived - _recomposite() rebuilds it from manual, subtract and the selected auto picks - so writing to it is pointless. Growing the composed result and baking into manualCanvas is the likely answer (same seam bakeAutoPicksInto() already uses), but check it against the MPI-371 layer-ORDER rule: auto picks union LAST, so a grow baked into manual must not resurrect something an erase removed.

Sequenced after MPI-380 by the user.

--- UNDO CONTRACT (MPI-376 shipped 2026-07-29) ---
MpiCanvas now owns a shared UndoStack and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z work on the mask layers. Any mutation of manualCanvas / subtractCanvas this card adds MUST record an undo entry or it silently punches a hole in Ctrl+Z. Layer-wide one-shot op -> mask._recordUndo() before mutating (after any early-return guard). Gesture -> undo.begin(mask.undoLayers()) at the start, undo.commit(mask.takeStrokeBox()) at the end, undo.abort() if nothing changed. READ docs/masking-undo.md FIRST.
Specific to this card: UndoStack.pendingLayer(i) already hands back the PRISTINE copy of a layer captured at begin() - that is exactly the anti-compounding drag-start snapshot this card needs, so do NOT build a second one. The bake on release is layer-wide, so it takes a full-rect _recordUndo() entry (~7.9MB on a 912x1140 layer, 18.9MB at MASK_MAX_EDGE) - measured, budget is 96MB.

MERGED 2026-08-01: this card absorbs MPI-400 (Mask Edge) and MPI-401 (mask/paint alpha brushes).
- MPI-400 - two sliders that turn the current mask into an outline - one expanding outward off the edge, one inward.
- MPI-401 - ten alpha brush textures, wired to both the mask brush and the paint brush.
WHY ONE CARD: All three add controls to the SAME shared MpiMaskStrip and all three are pixel operations over the same mask layers - grow/shrink and edge are the same dilate/erode primitive read two ways, and the brush pack is the strip's other half. Shipping them separately means rebuilding the strip three times.
The absorbed card(s) are closed as done/rejected - not built, kept as the record - and their full original text stays on disk at tasks/<id>/.

--- PICKED UP 2026-08-01, now step 1 of the MPI-424 umbrella ---
MPI-379 was rejected outright in the brainstorm the umbrella scheduled (canvas-side hover selection is complexity the user does not want; the thumb strip and Detect button stay), so this card leads instead. The user named both halves unprompted when asked what to pick up: the grow/shrink slider, and turning a mask into just its edges with TWO sliders - one expanding outward, one inward - which is the MPI-400 half absorbed into this card the same day. Both are the same primitive: an edge band is dilate(outward) minus erode(inward), so the threshold-blur mechanism is written once and read three ways. Design session in progress - do not implement before the design is agreed.
acceptance: One Grow / Shrink control in MpiMaskStrip, so every mask tool gets it in one place - centre is no change, right grows, left shrinks
The drag is live at the 1536 working size. If it is not, say so with a measurement and fall back to apply-on-release rather than shipping a laggy drag
Every frame is computed from a snapshot taken at drag start - dragging to 3, back to 0 and out to 3 again must produce exactly the same mask as going straight to 3
Returning the slider to centre restores the original mask bit-for-bit
The result is baked ONCE, on release, and the MPI-371 layer-order rule still holds afterwards (auto picks union last; a grow must not resurrect an erased region)
Shrink can empty the mask - the op strip must relock via evaluateMask() when it does, and the tool must not throw on an empty layer
Works on a mask built by any method (brush, points, detect) - it operates on layers, not on a source
New icon in js/utils/icons.js if one is needed; never paste raw SVG at the call site
docs/masking.md records the chosen mechanism and the compounding rule (200-line cap - trim first)
Every new mask/paint layer mutation records an UndoStack entry (docs/masking-undo.md) - an unwired mutation is a silent hole in Ctrl+Z
